title: AI foundations
summary: Understand the application around a model and identify where trust changes.
html:
Objectives

  • Describe tokens, context, embeddings, retrieval, and tool execution.
  • Identify who controls each input and which service enforces permission.
  • Record model and application versions so experiments can be repeated.

Concepts and boundaries

An AI application combines a probabilistic model with ordinary software: identity checks, retrieval, parsers, tools, and storage. Security depends on the boundaries between these components. A model response that sounds authoritative is still generated content. A downstream service must decide whether an action is permitted using authenticated identity and explicit policy.

Tokens are pieces of text consumed by a model. A context window contains the information available for one generation; it is not the same as persistent memory or the training dataset. Embeddings represent inputs as vectors for similarity tasks. Retrieval adds selected documents to context, while a tool call asks application code to perform an operation. Keep these mechanisms separate in your diagram: each gives an attacker different influence.

Practice checklist

Use an isolated lab or an explicitly authorized environment. Record prerequisites and configuration before changing inputs.

  1. Sketch a local or explicitly authorized sample assistant: user, application, model, document store, and tools.
  2. Label each arrow with the data type and the identity that controls it. Mark untrusted documents and generated outputs.
  3. Send a benign question and capture the application request, retrieval result, answer, and any tool invocation available in your lab logs.
  4. Repeat the same request several times. Record changes without assuming identical prompts guarantee identical outputs.

Expected observations

You should be able to distinguish a model answer from an authorized application action. Different outputs are observations, not proof of a security flaw. A finding needs an explicit violated boundary or unauthorized effect.

Mitigations and retesting

Keep authorization in deterministic application code, minimize tool privileges, and treat retrieved text and generated content as untrusted inputs. Log enough context to reproduce a finding without storing unnecessary secrets.
